name: Test7
description: Conceptual data model for a human management system covering people, recruitment, employment, payroll, time/attendance, benefits, performance, learning, assets and lifecycle events.

metadata.Description: An individual as a general actor in the model — any natural person referenced by the organization (employees, candidates, contacts, dependents).
A person engaged by the organization under an employment relationship who performs work and is managed by the company.
A person applying or being considered for a role or opportunity within the organization, typically during recruitment.
A defined set of responsibilities and requirements describing a role that can be filled by an individual within the organization.
A specific vacancy or available assignment that the organization seeks to fill, usually tied to a job position.
A formal organizational unit grouping related functions, responsibilities, or staff within the company.
A group of people organized to work together on shared tasks or objectives, often cross-functional or project-based.
A set of responsibilities or expected behaviors assigned to a person in a given context, distinct from a specific job position.
A person responsible for supervising, directing, and evaluating others' work and often accountable for a team or function.
A formal agreement defining the terms and conditions of employment between the organization and a worker.
A classification that defines compensation range or level for jobs, used to standardize salary structure.
A record of payments, deductions, and payroll-related transactions for an individual across pay periods.
A structured package of non-salary compensation offerings (insurance, retirement, perks) available to eligible persons.
The act or record of an individual selecting and being registered for one or more benefit plan options.
A historical or current record of an individual's base pay and compensation changes over time.
A record capturing hours worked, tasks performed, or time allocation for payroll and tracking purposes.
A log of presence, absence, check-ins/outs, and attendance-related events for scheduling and compliance.
A formal request by an individual to take time away from work for vacation, illness, or other approved reasons.
A scheduled block of working time assigned to a person, often used in hourly or round-the-clock operations.
A physical site, facility, or workplace address where organizational activities are performed.
Any physical or logical asset owned or managed by the organization that has value and is used in operations.
A person designated to be notified in case of an emergency involving an individual associated with the organization.
metadata.Synonyms: ["Next of Kin","Emergency Contact Person","Emergency Contact Info"]

metadata.Description: A formal assessment of an individual's job performance, typically used for feedback, development, and compensation decisions.
A specific, measurable objective assigned to an individual or team to guide performance and development.
A measurable capability or combination of skills, knowledge, and behaviors required to perform effectively in a role.
A specific learned ability or expertise that enables a person to perform tasks or duties.
A structured learning offering designed to build knowledge, skills, or competencies for individuals or groups.
The record of an individual's registration or participation in a training course or program.
A formal credential awarded to an individual recognizing attainment of specified skills, knowledge, or standards.
A structured interaction used to evaluate a candidate's suitability for a role, often part of recruitment.
A written document presenting employment terms and a formal invitation for a candidate to accept a job.
A process of verifying an individual's history (employment, criminal, education) to assess suitability or risk.
A record documenting the end of an individual's employment, including reasons, dates, and exit details.
A discrete activity or checklist item completed to integrate a new hire into the organization and make them operational.
